units.translation: 336. 〈to the shores:〉 it is written "to the seas." Lᵐ

338-49a. 〈There:〉 In that place, he says, the Argonauts, fearing the multitude of the Colchians, yielded to them and wished to keep the fleece and not hand it over, but to entrust Medea—for the justice concerning her was disputed—to Artemis in her temple, until someone should judge whether she ought to be given back to her father or to the Argonauts. L
temple, until someone should judge whether she ought to be given back to her father or to the Argonauts. L
b. 〈by agreement:〉 by reconciliation. Gᶢ
373-75. 〈Or you then:〉 Reproaching Jason, she says that he should kill her with a sword, so that she may receive a worthy return for her love for him. She said this in character. L
380. 〈wretchedly:〉 laboriously. Gᶢ
384. being distressed: instead of "being worn out and tortured." Lᵐ P
387. by your fickleness: by your evil disposition and thoughtlessness, because you swore falsely. Lᵐ (P)
406. 〈Truly:〉 desirable things. Gᶢ Sᵐ
411-13. 〈with unseemly:〉 For in the face of evils, she says, one must plan evils. She has therefore chosen to kill Apsyrtus as well, on account of the sins previously committed by her. Lᵐ
417-18. 〈If somehow:〉 If somehow, she says, I could persuade Apsyrtus to come alone to me alone, having made a pact of friendship with him. Lᵐ
425. Dia: on Naxos. Callimachus (fr. 165 Schn.): "in Dia; for that was the older name for Naxos." Lᵐ P
428-29a. with embroideries: with ornaments. Lᵐ (P)
b. not touching it: in no way could you satisfy your desire by touching or beholding that robe. Lᵐ
432. tipsy: extremely drunk with unmixed wine or nectar. Lᵐ (P)
433. daughter of Minos: Ariadne. Lᶢ (P)
445. 〈great abomination:〉 He says that love is a great abomination to humans. L

459-62. alone and face to face: Apsyrtus, going alone to Medea, was testing whether, being still tender and inexperienced in wiles, she might wish to betray the Argonauts, not knowing the plot against himself. L
465-67. she turned her eyes away: Medea turned away from Apsyrtus as he was being killed, so as not to see his murder. L
468. 〈And him, like an ox-slayer:〉 Jason struck Apsyrtus like someone felling an ox. L
470. Brygi: a people of Illyria.
471. 〈in the forecourt:〉 He used "forecourt" loosely for the pronaos.
473-74. 〈her veil:〉 As Apsyrtus was dying, he stained Medea's veil and robe with his own blood. L

477-79. cut from the dead: Those who killed by treachery in ancient times would cut off certain extremities of the slain and, taking them, would hang them from his neck. Of the so-called extremities 〈...〉 countless and many appendages. Then, taking his blood, they spat it out three times into their mouths. They did this to expiate the treacherous murder.

481. Apsyrtians: a people named after Apsyrtus.
